newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends below key 6000 level, oil stocks slip.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends below key 6000 level, oil stocks slip.

text.p: The Dow industrials gyrated to a weaker finish, closing below the key 6000 level for the first time in two weeks as traders stepped up profit-taking in oil stocks and other recent high-flyers.

"We started a correction on Monday and we're still in it. It's a backing and filling affair that might wear people out for a week or two instead of a fast nosebleed," said Alfred Goldman of A.G. Edwards. "We have profit-taking in integrated oil, household products and food--areas that had been strong."
The Dow lost 44 to about 5992, its fourth consecutive loss.
The blue chip index slid 58 points over the first three days of the week. It was the Dow's first close below 6000 since October 10.
The Dow rode a wild rollercoaster in the afternoon as Birinyi Associates Inc tracked three buy and four sell programs.
The Nasdaq Composite gave up earlier gains and lost one to about 1227. The S&P 500 fell five to about 702.
Losers outpaced gainers 12-11 on heavy NYSE volume of about 415 million shares.
Stocks were pressured from the opening bell by weak bonds.

The long bond lost 9/32 to yield 6.85 percent after weekly jobless claims fell more than expected to 320,000 for the week ended October 19. The data suggested that the nation's labor market remains tight.

Oil stocks fell as December NYMEX crude fell $0.35 to $24.51 a barrel amid prospects of a larger total distillate supply. Worries of a shortage had helped lift crude to a post-Gulf War high of above $26 a barrel. Among the Dow components, Texaco slumped 2-7/8 to 100-3/4, Exxon was off 1-3/8 to 87-1/4 and Chevron lost 3/4 to 66-1/2.
Another Dow component, Procter & Gamble lost 2-1/4 to 94.
The consumer products giant reported record fiscal first-quarter earnings but a decline in worldwide sales due to the strong dollar.

Goldman, technical research director at A.G. Edwards, said the market was taking a "normal pause to refresh. There's the excuse that the market is concerned about a possible loss of the House to the Democrats. The reality is the Dow is up 18 percent since July and 10 percent since Labor Day."
"People are itchy to take profits. It's easy to rationalize. It's a choppy, marking time day," said Robert Stovall, president of Stovall/Twenty-First.
Wall Street is awaiting Friday's release of September U.S. durable goods. A 2.0 percent increase is anticipated.

Among individual shares, Dow component United Technologies surged 4-1/8 to 127-5/8. The company on Wednesday reported a jump in quarterly profits and forecast earnings will grow by 15 percent in 1997. Several brokers raises earnings estimates.
Alcoa, another member of the Dow, added 1-7/8 to 59-7/8. Morgan Stanley raised the stock to strong buy from outperform.
Lucent rose 1-5/8 to 50 after hitting a new high of 51 intraday. The company reported fiscal fourth-quarter earnings of $0.40, topping the Street consensus of $0.37.

AMP Inc slumped 3-1/4 to 35 after reporting a drop in third-quarter earnings and said "significant price erosion" in personal computers and communications will pressure fourth- quarter results. Merrill and Smith Barney cut the stock.

Shares of computer disk drive manufacturers were stronger after Read-Rite and Western Digital reported healthy quarters. Read-Rite added 1/2 to 17-7/8, Western Digital rose 2-3/4 to 48-1/4 and Seagate Technology added 2-3/8 to 65-7/8.
Electronic Arts surged 4-1/8 to 37-1/2 after reporting a near doubling in quarterly results. Alex Brown upgraded the stock.
Newbridge Networks lost 2-1/2 to 31 in U.S. trading on earnings jitters, industry analysts said.
James River surged 3-1/2 to 31-5/8 after reporting a jump in quarterly profits.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.88 to 1227.00.
The S&P 500 index fell 4.98 to 702.29.
(Figures official as of 1645 EDT/2045 GMT)
-- Wall Street desk 212 859 1721
